findings.title: retain_runner_status checks against the live runner status, so the copy is dropped when the runner's status changed after the copy, including for the 'Runner dpkg database differs from its copied status' refusal
findings.description: retain_runner_status() keeps work/apt/status only when it is byte-identical to the live DPKG_STATUS at the moment the finally block runs. That is after apt-get update and the download, which can take up to about 18 minutes. The rule does exclude apt_config's empty placeholder. It also drops the private copy that apt and the walk really used whenever /var/lib/dpkg/status changed after the copy. That is exactly the case the refusal 'Runner dpkg database differs from its copied status' exists to catch. So for that refusal the candidate retains no runner-dpkg-status. Two records are then false. TEST_EVIDENCE.md:12722 says 'The candidate retains the status it used, also when resolution refuses after the runner's status was copied.' The code comment at windows11_candidate.py:354-355 says 'Retained even when resolution refuses, so a refusal can be traced to the runner package that caused it.' There is also a second effect, which still fails closed. A resolution can succeed because every recorded row agreed with dpkg-query, yet be refused anyway if any unrelated byte of the live status changed. The refusal is an unnamed FileNotFoundError carrying an absolute path, not the named 'Retained runner dpkg status differs from the resolution'. Possible fixes: decide on retention from the digest taken at copy time, or a flag set after the copy, not from the live file; or reword the two records. The trigger is unlikely on a hosted runner, so this is a records and diagnosability defect only.
findings.evidence: Probe in my own copy (review4-work/retain-lens/probes/test_review4_probe.py). It ran it from copy/scripts/tests, then I moved it out. It drives the real windows11_candidate.main() through the test module's run_candidate(), with the REAL ubuntu_gnome_prepare.resolve() and runner_provided(). The candidate's resolve is wrapped to use resolve_fixture-style fakes for apt_config and the owner. The live runner status is rewritten to LIVE_AFTER_COPY at apt-get time, as in resolve_fixture. Output: `PROBE 2.39-0ubuntu8.7 1 CANDIDATE_FAILED 'Runner dpkg database differs from its copied status: libc6' error_type ValueError | runner-dpkg-status retained: False | retain() called: True | dpkg-query ran: True`. With dpkg-query agreeing with the copy: `PROBE 2.39-0ubuntu8.6 1 CANDIDATE_FAILED "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../output/runner-dpkg-status'" error_type FileNotFoundError | runner-dpkg-status retained: False`. Code: windows11_candidate.py:200-205 compares `private.read_bytes() == DPKG_STATUS.read_bytes()` at finally time; ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:324-325 copies once, before apt runs.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. It reproduces, nothing already handles it, and the false record sentences are real defects under the "every record sentence exactly true" standard. It still fails closed, so nonblocking is the right severity.

Code facts, read in the uncommitted tree:
- In scripts/linux_gnome/ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py, resolve() runs apt_config first, which writes the empty placeholder. It then copies DPKG_STATUS to root/status once, at lines 325-328, before `apt-get update` (180 s) and the download (900 s).
- runner_provided() runs last. It raises "Runner dpkg database differs from its copied status" when dpkg-query's live rows disagree with the copy.
- In scripts/windows11/windows11_candidate.py, retain_runner_status() at lines 191-208 runs in the finally at lines 351-356, after resolve returns or raises. It copies the private status only if it is byte-identical to the live DPKG_STATUS at that moment.
- So whenever the live /var/lib/dpkg/status changed after the copy, the status that apt and the walk used is dropped. That is the usual cause of the "differs" refusal: dpkg rewrites status when it changes a package.
- On the success path the same change makes `digest(args.output / "runner-dpkg-status")` at line 357 raise an unnamed FileNotFoundError with an absolute path. The named "Retained runner dpkg status differs from the resolution" refusal never fires. This still fails closed.

Independent reproduction in my own copy, review4-work/refute-retain/copy/scripts/tests/test_refute_probe.py:
- The probe wraps the harness's resolve through run_candidate() and rewrites the live DPKG_STATUS after the copy.
- Raising the "differs" refusal gave `1 CANDIDATE_FAILED ValueError 'Runner dpkg database differs from its copied status: libpcre2-8-0' retained: False in retained/: False`.
- With no refusal it gave `1 CANDIDATE_FAILED FileNotFoundError "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '.../output/runner-dpkg-status'" retained: False`.

Not already handled:
- No test or mutant covers a live status that changes after the copy. The candidate tests only cover a refusal before the copy and a refusal after it, both with the live status unchanged. The mutants only remove the retain call or the digest check.

The records make an unqualified claim:
- TEST_EVIDENCE.md: "The candidate retains the status it used, also when resolution refuses after the runner's status was copied."
- TEST_EVIDENCE.md and the review README line 65: "the candidate keeps the runner status when resolution refuses."
- The code comment at windows11_candidate.py:354-355: "Retained even when resolution refuses, so a refusal can be traced to the runner package that caused it."
- Only the retain_runner_status docstring ("Only a status byte-identical to the runner's own is retained") and README line 72 state the byte-identity condition, and neither mentions the case where the live status changes.

Edge cases that do not save the claim:
- The "differs" refusal can fire with the status file unchanged, when dpkg's updates journal holds pending entries. In that case the copy is retained.
- That refusal's message also names up to 10 changed packages, which partly covers traceability.
- Neither makes the universal record sentences true. A trigger on a hosted runner is unlikely, so this is a records and diagnosability defect. It is not a safety defect.

I could not refute this. I reproduced it in my own copy (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tanishkalwad-jobapplyv2/17ee071f-b2d5-4e6f-a57e-209b35ae06c1/scratchpad/review4-work/refute-retain-live/copy). The repository tree is unchanged: still 16 entries in `git status --short`.

How the code behaves:
- resolve(..., runner_status=True) in scripts/linux_gnome/ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:325-328 copies /var/lib/dpkg/status once, before apt-get update (180 s budget) and the download (900 s budget).
- runner_provided raises "Runner dpkg database differs from its copied status" when live dpkg-query rows disagree with that copy. dpkg-query reads the live dpkg database.
- retain_runner_status (scripts/windows11/windows11_candidate.py:191-208) runs in the finally block at line 353. It copies work/apt/status to runner-dpkg-status only when the copy is byte-identical to the live DPKG_STATUS at that moment.
- So a change to the live status file at any point after the copy drops the retention. That change is also the usual cause of the "differs" refusal.

Probe 1, test_probe_refute_retain_live.py, drives the real main() through the test module's run_candidate:
- "differs" refusal, live status unchanged: runner-dpkg-status retained: True.
- Same refusal, live status changed after the copy: retained: False.
- Successful resolution, unrelated live bytes changed: CANDIDATE_FAILED with FileNotFoundError "[Errno 2] No such file or directory: '<abs>/output/runner-dpkg-status'", not the named "Retained runner dpkg status differs from the resolution".

Probe 2, test_probe_refute_retain_real.py, uses the REAL prepare.resolve() and runner_provided(), with a fake dpkg-query that reads the live status file:
- A recorded row (libc6) changed during apt: "Runner dpkg database differs from its copied status: libc6", retained: False.
- An unrelated row changed: resolution succeeds, then FileNotFoundError, retained: False.
- No change: resolution passes and the status is retained. The run then fails at the simulated install only because the fixture's plan lists qemu-utils, which my lock lacks; that is irrelevant here.

Records that are not exactly true:
- docs/TEST_EVIDENCE.md:12722 says "The candidate retains the status it used, also when resolution refuses after the runner's status was copied." This is false whenever the live status changed after the copy, which is the main trigger of the "differs" refusal.
- The comment at windows11_candidate.py:354-355 says "Retained even when resolution refuses, so a refusal can be traced to the runner package that caused it." It is false for the same case.
- No record says retention depends on the live status being unchanged. grep finds only "byte-identical to the runner's own", in the review README and TEST_EVIDENCE:12742.

One small overstatement in the finding: if dpkg has pending entries in its updates/ journal that are not yet written to the status file, dpkg-query can differ while the status bytes are unchanged. The copy would then be retained, so "for that refusal the candidate retains no runner-dpkg-status" holds in the usual case rather than always. This does not change the defect.

The finding's own assessment stands. Every path fails closed: the unrelated-change case refuses, though with an unnamed FileNotFoundError. The trigger is unlikely on a hosted runner. This is a nonblocking defect in the records and in how easy a refusal is to diagnose. It is real and has not been dealt with.

findings.title: Review-3 critic-1 fix says Essential packages are 'not walked' / 'not recorded', but dpkg and tar are Essential and are walked, recorded and re-checked
findings.description:
The fix for review 3's Essential-package finding added a categorical sentence in several places, and it is false:
- runner_provided docstring: 'Essential packages, which packages need not declare, are not walked; like everything else on the image, they are bound only through the runner image version.'
- KI-0189 (KNOWN_ISSUES.md:72): 'Essential packages need not be declared, so they are not walked; as before, they are bound only through the runner image version.'
- ADR-0009 implementation note (DECISIONS.md:484): 'Essential packages need not be declared, so they are not recorded and stay bound only through the image version.'
- TEST_EVIDENCE.md:12744 and the packet README:73 say the records now state that Essential packages are bound only through the image version.

The walk follows declared relations and does not special-case Essential packages. So an Essential package that a walked package declares is walked, recorded in runner_provided_packages, and re-checked by the campaign's require_runner_packages, not bound only by ImageVersion. One of review 3's own refuters already noted this ('dpkg and tar are walked, recorded and re-checked'). The accurate statement is narrower: Essential packages that no walked package declares are not recorded.
findings.evidence: Parsed round 53's real runner status (scratchpad/hostclosure-41929794476/art/runner-dpkg-status) against docs/evidence/m03-native-runtime-diagnostics/windows-host-closure/round53-41929794476/runner-status-lock.json. It has 23 installed Essential packages, and two of them are in runner_provided_packages: `dpkg {'version': '1.22.6ubuntu6.6', 'architecture': 'amd64', 'status': 'install ok installed'}` and `tar {'version': '1.35+dfsg-3ubuntu0.4', ...}`, both 'Essential: yes'. dpkg is declared by python3-minimal (Pre-Depends), and tar is declared by dpkg (Depends). The round 51, 52 and 53 locks each hold 88 rows, and dpkg and tar are in all three.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. I checked everything read-only and created no files.

1. The code does not exempt Essential packages. In scripts/linux_gnome/ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py, runner_provided (lines 224-283) walks the Pre-Depends and Depends groups of every downloaded control and of every installed package it reaches. Every runner package that provides a name in a group is added to `provided` and then walked itself. Nothing checks the Essential field, so an Essential package is walked like any other once a walked package declares it.

2. The real runner data agrees.
   - round53's real status (hostclosure-41929794476/art/runner-dpkg-status) has 23 installed packages with 'Essential: yes'. dpkg (1.22.6ubuntu6.6) and tar (1.35+dfsg-3ubuntu0.4) are both 'Essential: yes' and 'install ok installed'.
   - On the runner, dpkg's own control has `Depends: tar (>= 1.28-1)`.
   - The runner-status-lock.json for rounds 51, 52 and 53 each holds 88 runner_provided_packages, and dpkg and tar are in all three. Only the walk adds rows, so both were walked and recorded.

3. The recorded rows are re-checked at the campaign. In windows11_vm.py, install_tools calls require_runner_packages(owner, reviewed, ...), and that compares runner_packages(owner, sorted(reviewed)) with the reviewed rows. So dpkg and tar are bound by an exact live dpkg check as well as by the image version, not only by the image version.

4. These record sentences are categorical and false for dpkg and tar:
   - ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:231-233: "Essential packages, which packages need not declare, are not walked". The commas make the clause non-restrictive, so the sentence covers all Essential packages.
   - KNOWN_ISSUES.md:72: "Essential packages need not be declared, so they are not walked".
   - DECISIONS.md:484: "so they are not recorded and stay bound only through the image version". The locks directly contradict this.
   - TEST_EVIDENCE.md:12744 and the review README:73 repeat that Essential packages are bound only through the image version.

5. Review 3's own evidence says the same: "only dpkg and tar are among the 88 rows".

The accurate statement is narrower: Essential packages that no walked package declares are not recorded, and only the image version binds them. The finding is real. It is a record-accuracy defect rather than a code defect, so its nonblocking severity is fair. It still fails the standard that every record sentence is exactly true.

I could not refute this. The finding is true and reproducible.

Code: runner_provided() in scripts/linux_gnome/ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py (lines 223-280) walks Pre-Depends and Depends through runner.get(name, []) for every name in a group. It never checks the Essential field. Any installed package that some walked package declares, Essential or not, is added to `provided`, pushed onto `pending` and walked in turn. It then becomes a lock row. In windows11_vm.py, reviewed_runner_packages() takes every row, and require_runner_packages() re-checks them against live dpkg before and after install. So the docstring's sentence is literally false for declared Essential packages: "Essential packages, which packages need not declare, are not walked; like everything else on the image, they are bound only through the runner image version". The comma-delimited, non-restrictive clause makes it a statement about all Essential packages.

Real-runner data: I parsed scratchpad/hostclosure-41929794476/art/runner-dpkg-status. It has 23 installed Essential packages. Two of them, dpkg (1.22.6ubuntu6.6) and tar (1.35+dfsg-3ubuntu0.4), appear in runner_provided_packages in all three committed locks (round51, round52 and round53 runner-status-lock.json, 88 rows each). python3-minimal declares `Depends: dpkg (>= 1.13.20)`, and dpkg declares `Depends: tar (>= 1.28-1)`. No Essential package is in the downloaded `packages`. (On the dependency type the finding is slightly off: python3-minimal declares dpkg in Depends, not Pre-Depends. That does not change the conclusion.)

Synthetic check in my own copy: I ran runner_provided() with a stubbed installed_rows on a status holding python3-minimal -> dpkg (Essential) -> tar (Essential), plus an undeclared Essential sed. The result was ['dpkg', 'python3-minimal', 'tar']. The declared Essential packages are walked and recorded; only the undeclared one (sed) is left out. Script: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tanishkalwad-jobapplyv2/17ee071f-b2d5-4e6f-a57e-209b35ae06c1/scratchpad/review4-work/essential-refuter/check/walk.py

Records that carry the false categorical claim:
- docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md:72: "Essential packages need not be declared, so they are not walked"
- docs/DECISIONS.md:484: "so they are not recorded and stay bound only through the image version"
- docs/evidence/m03-w07-adr0009-host-closure-review/README.md:73: "since Essential packages are bound only through the image version"
- docs/TEST_EVIDENCE.md:12744 correctly reports what the records say, but it endorses a false statement as a fix.

The accurate statement is narrower: Essential packages that no walked package declares are not recorded and are bound only through ImageVersion; declared ones, such as dpkg and tar, are recorded and re-checked. The defect is in the records and docstring only; behavior fails closed. That fits a nonblocking severity, but it breaks the "every record sentence exactly true" standard.

findings.title: closed_install_plan docstring: 'only its roots can be such a package' is false; acl and python3 pin exact-version dependencies that the image carries
findings.description:
The rewritten docstring, the fix for review 3's critic-3, says: 'The Windows host lock is resolved against the runner's own status (ADR-0009), so only its roots can be such a package [a version of a package the runner image already carries]: a root the image carries (acl, python3) at the locked version is left as installed, and one the archive has updated would replace it'. The scenario it describes is an archive update to acl or python3, which is the KI-0189 limit. In that scenario, non-root packages the image carries also enter the lock at new versions, because these roots depend on exact versions:
- acl depends on `libacl1 (= <its version>)`;
- python3 Pre-Depends on `python3-minimal (=)` and depends on `libpython3-stdlib (=)`.

All three dependencies are installed on the runner. Resolving the updated root against the runner's status therefore makes apt upgrade and download them too. More generally, any updated root with a raised versioned dependency on a runner library does the same. KI-0189:71's 'It downloads every root, and only those dependencies that the runner image lacks' and the module docstring at ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:7-8 make the same overstatement for this scenario, unless 'lacks' is read as 'lacks at the required version'. The prepare still fails closed, because closed_install_plan refuses the upgrade lines. Only the docstring is untrue.
findings.evidence: dpkg-deb -f command records in round 53's runner-status artifact (scratchpad/hostclosure-41929794476/art/runner-status): command-003 gives `Package: acl / Version: 2.3.2-1build1.1 / Depends: libacl1 (= 2.3.2-1build1.1), libc6 (>= 2.38)`. command-041 gives `Package: python3 / Version: 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1 / Pre-Depends: python3-minimal (= 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1) / Depends: python3.12 (>= 3.12.3-0~), libpython3-stdlib (= 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1)`. The same job's runner-dpkg-status lists libacl1 2.3.2-1build1.1, python3-minimal 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1 and libpython3-stdlib 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1 as 'install ok installed'.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding holds: the docstring makes a false claim, and the code still fails closed.

1. The quoted text is at the cited line. Lines 119-125 of scripts/linux_gnome/ubuntu_gnome_host.py (uncommitted diff) say: "The Windows host lock is resolved against the runner's own status (ADR-0009), so only its roots can be such a package ... one the archive has updated would replace it". In context, "such a package" means a version, held in the lock, of a package the runner image already carries.

2. The evidence cited in the finding is exact. In hostclosure-41929794476/art/runner-status:
   - command-003.stdout: acl 2.3.2-1build1.1 has `Depends: libacl1 (= 2.3.2-1build1.1), libc6 (>= 2.38)`.
   - command-041.stdout: python3 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1 has `Pre-Depends: python3-minimal (= 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1)` and `Depends: python3.12 (>= 3.12.3-0~), libpython3-stdlib (= 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1)`.
   - runner-dpkg-status lists libacl1 2.3.2-1build1.1, python3-minimal 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1 and libpython3-stdlib 3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1, each amd64 and "install ok installed".

3. Apt would download the dependencies too. resolve(..., runner_status=True) runs `apt-get --download-only --reinstall install <roots>` against the copied runner status. The retained apt source, scratchpad/private-install.cc lines 1083-1099, shows how a root with a newer candidate is handled:
   - MarkInstall marks the candidate for upgrade, so State.Install() is true and the reinstall branch is skipped.
   - The root then goes into doAutoInstallLater, which resolves its dependencies.
   - An exact `(=)` dependency on an installed library at the old version is not satisfied, so apt upgrades that library to its candidate, and download-only fetches it.
   - So an archive update to acl puts libacl1 in the lock at a new version. An update to python3 does the same for python3-minimal and libpython3-stdlib. None of these is a root.
   - More generally, any newly resolved package with a raised versioned dependency on an installed runner library has the same effect.
   - Review 1 (review-1-workflow-result.json) already stated this for a python3-defaults update: "python3-minimal, libpython3-stdlib and python3-dev would be upgraded too".

4. Nothing in the code prevents this:
   - resolve() has no check that refuses downloaded non-roots already on the runner.
   - runner_provided() skips packages that are in `controls`.
   - reviewed_runner_packages only refuses a package that is both locked and runner-provided.

5. It still fails closed. The plan lines for these upgrades take the form "Inst libacl1 [old] (new ...)", which PLAN_ADD cannot match because the bracket comes before the parenthesis. closed_install_plan therefore refuses them, and simulate_host_install refuses the candidate before stage_host. Only the sentence is untrue.

6. The related records:
   - KI-0189 line 71 and the module docstring of ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py (lines 7-8) say it downloads "only those dependencies the runner image lacks".
